analysis:
The PR is documentation-only. It adds a DARKBLOOM_TTFT_GDN_BLOCKED row to the LaunchAgent passthrough table (docs/provider/cli-reference.md line 1741) and a matching row in docs/reference/configuration.md (line 414). It describes a tuning environment variable selecting the Gated DeltaNet prompt-window kernel for qwen3_5, qwen3_5_moe and prism_hadamard_qwen35. The variable is read once per process and forwarded to the LaunchAgent.

Security relevance examined:
- It is a performance/kernel-selection flag only. It does not touch attestation (TB-009/TB-011), the coordinator WebSocket (TB-002), key custody (A-002/A-003), or the prefix cache storage (T-041).
- Forwarding an env var into the plist adds no new secret or privilege. It is the same operator-controlled local boundary as the other passthrough entries. The provider operator is already the adversary in TB-003, and kernel selection is within their control anyway.
- Doc claims: the default probe keeps a four-row kernel only where it reproduces gated_delta_step bit for bit. Forced kernels (`packed`/`rows`) skip that check and are for A/B measurement only. This is accurately flagged as a risk to output correctness, which is consistent with T-007 and T-056 (no runtime secrecy or correct-computation claim). The documentation does not overclaim correctness.
- Residual question: the forced kernels could produce divergent outputs if an operator uses them in production. That is operator-controlled and already covered by the T-007 accepted risk. The underlying source (GatedDelta.swift) was not supplied, so the claimed passthrough and probe behavior is unverified. Nothing in the docs indicates a security regression.
- The second unit (configuration.md) was supplied only as metadata plus a truncated patch. The changed line is a single table row and appears consistent with the cli-reference row.

No findings. No threat-model update is needed.
